standard_prerequisites.name: Quasi-inverses and equivalences
standard_prerequisites.statement: A function is an equivalence as soon as it has a two-sided homotopy inverse, and conversely.
standard_prerequisites.use: Both cases in the proof are settled by exhibiting an explicit quasi-inverse.

standard_prerequisites.name: Homotopy inverses of equivalences
standard_prerequisites.statement: If e is an equivalence then its inverse opp(e) satisfies the two homotopy identities.
standard_prerequisites.use: The candidate quasi-inverses are built from opp(g o f) composed with g or f.

standard_prerequisites.name: Closure of equivalences under composition
standard_prerequisites.statement: A composite of two equivalences is an equivalence.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is recalled in the retained lead-in and covers the case in which f and g themselves are the given equivalences.

core_obligations: Assume g o f and g are equivalences and exhibit opp(g o f) o g as a quasi-inverse to f (source line 618).
Verify the first homotopy: opp(g o f) o g o f is homotopic to the identity on A because opp(g o f) is a left inverse of g o f (source line 619).
Verify the second homotopy by the displayed three-step chain, rewriting f o opp(g o f) o g through the inverse identities of g and g o f until it becomes the identity on B (source lines 620-625).
Treat the symmetric case: if g o f and f are equivalences then f o opp(g o f) is a quasi-inverse to g (source line 626).

proof_roadmap.step: First case: build the quasi-inverse of f and check one homotopy.
Check the other homotopy by the displayed chain.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Theorem 4.7.1 at source lines 612-616: if any two of f : A -> B, g : B -> C and g o f are equivalences then so is the third. The author's proof (source lines 617-627) is an explicit quasi-inverse construction rather than a citation: in the case where g o f and g are equivalences it proposes opp(g o f) o g as a quasi-inverse to f (line 618), checks the easy homotopy on A (line 619), and then has to verify the homotopy on B through the three-step chain displayed at lines 620-625 in which the inverse identities of g and of g o f are used in a specific order; the symmetric case, with f o opp(g o f) as a quasi-inverse to g, is stated at line 626. The retained lead-in supplies the composition closure that covers the remaining configuration. The statement is a single implication and records none of the quasi-inverse formulas.
